report.answer_text:
Baby KJ Muldoon received a custom CRISPR base-editing therapy designed to correct a specific mutation in his *CPS1* gene. The treatment used lipid nanoparticles to deliver the editor to his liver cells. KJ was born with severe carbamoyl phosphate synthetase 1 (CPS1) deficiency, a rare disorder that prevents the body from clearing toxic ammonia. (beta.nih.gov)
He received his first dose on February 25, 2025, at Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia, becoming the first person to receive a CRISPR therapy tailored to their individual mutation. (chop.edu)
